tweets.text:
i started bidding and buying here.

not because things have changed. actually, not much has. but something important did.

we're still following equities. the Fed is still ahead of us, macro is a mess, and there's enough geopolitical risk out there to send bitcoin down $5k in a single candle.

i still think we could see $75k, maybe even lower if someone big capitulates and takes everyone down with them.

but here's what's interesting.

the same people who were calling for $100k are now shorting $80k. every influencer suddenly has a very convincing explanation for why we need to go lower.
and after all the shit we've been through, bitcoin is still around $80k.

that's worth paying attention to.

one positive headline or stocks ticking up and we're back at $83k, $85k. maybe even $90k before the next bad headline hits.

imagine everyone waiting for the big capitulation candle, and when it finally comes, bitcoin dumps from $90k to $85k instead of $80k to $75k.

the level everyone was terrified of becomes support.

and the same people shorting $80k will be explaining why $100k was inevitable.

i'm not calling the bottom. but I started buying again.

tweets.text:
Look at $ETH today.

Sure, the market is weak. But let’s not pretend the Ethereum Foundation’s actions don’t matter.

Once again, it feels like $ETH holders are getting the middle finger.

Instead of selling, how about doing something that actually captures value?

Let me be clear, I’m holding a shit ton of $ETH and $BMNR. I’m not selling.

But I’m seriously done with this kind of shit. If you want people to believe in Ethereum, start acting like the token holders matter.

quote.text:
In all honesty, seeing the Ethereum Foundation sell $ETH again is incredibly frustrating.

I love Ethereum. I love the chain. But why are we constantly selling the asset instead of doing more to increase its value?

Start thinking seriously about buybacks. Create stronger incentives for L2s to accumulate and buy back $ETH. Improve ETH value capture.

The ecosystem is incredible. Now we need the economics of the token to reflect that.

tweets.text:
I think we’re entering an interesting phase for AI trading, where trust is becoming just as important as performance.

Hacken’s research shows that 84.8% of surveyed crypto traders have already used AI for research or trading.

But there’s still a clear line when it comes to giving AI control, only 6.5% would let it manage more than half of their account.

What caught my attention is that @MEXC found willingness to automate increases from 55% to 71.8% when proper risk limits are in place.

And 95.5% want at least one mandatory safeguard.

For me, that says a lot: people aren’t against AI taking control. They just want to know there are guardrails.

The future of AI trading may be less about full autonomy and more about controlled autonomy. Do you agree?
